key_insight: SearchOS makes open-domain search agents more robust by turning implicit search progress into explicit shared state, preventing repetitive failure loops and improving task coverage.
engineering_relevance: The system offers a practical multi-agent orchestration pattern for long-horizon web search, with state tracking, stall detection, and scheduling mechanisms that can improve throughput and reliability in deployed information-seeking workflows.
method: Reformulates information seeking as relational schema completion with grounded citations.
Uses Search-Oriented Context Management (SOCM) to maintain Frontier Task, Evidence Graph, Coverage Map, and Failure Memory.
Adds a middleware harness and pipeline-parallel scheduler to monitor stalls, record evidence, and refill unresolved tasks with reusable skills.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that SearchOS leads all metrics on the WideSearch and GISA benchmarks against evaluated single- and multi-agent baselines.
watch_item: The added control and state-management layers may increase system complexity and integration overhead, especially when scaling to heterogeneous tools or noisy web sources.
paper_title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
